cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: What Are We Now?
cards.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded my towel beside yours. Nice and ready for visitors. Shall I put my washbag in the guest cupboard too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I folded mine because the hook broke. Your old towel is still on your hook.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the broken hook. Shall I use the old towel when I stay tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Use it. I haven't given that space to anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I leave, do you want it back on my hook or with the guest laundry?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 confidently copies folding as visitor preparation; A3 covers broken-hook correction while asking old-towel use; A5 tests whether place persists.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 distinguishes old place from guest pile; A3 asks use; B4 retained space drives A5 storage choice.

relationship.evidence: B2 gives household facts and B4 offers meaningful reassurance.

heightening.evidence: A5 develops B4 nobody-else statement into a future belonging test.

specificity.evidence: A1 towel/guest cupboard and B2 old hook locate interaction.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 concrete hook versus laundry question avoids directly asking a label.
